html:
The Congress of Vienna was a meeting of European states in Vienna from September 1814 to June 1815 that redrew the map of Europe after the wars of Napoleon. Its final act was signed on 9 June 1815, nine days before Waterloo.

The great powers ran it: the Austrian Empire, whose foreign minister Metternich was host, Britain, Russia and Prussia, with defeated France let in through its minister Talleyrand. They wanted a balance of power, so that no one state could dominate again, and the return of old ruling houses.

Main results:

  • The Holy Roman Empire was not revived. A loose German Confederation of 39 states took its place, and Prussia gained land on the Rhine and part of Saxony.
  • Austria got Lombardy and Venetia, and the pope got back the Papal States.
  • The Dutch king got the old Austrian Netherlands (Belgium) and became grand duke of Luxembourg.
  • Switzerland's borders were fixed and its neutrality backed by the powers.
  • Russia kept most of Poland as a kingdom under the tsar.
  • The powers condemned the slave trade, though they set no date to end it.

The settlement, kept up by meetings of the powers called the Concert of Europe, held off a general European war until 1914. The revolutions of 1848 and the unification of Italy and of Germany undid much of its map.
sum: The Congress of Vienna was a meeting of European states in Vienna from September 1814 to June 1815 that redrew the map of Europe after the wars of Napoleon. Its final act was signed on 9 June 1815, nine days before Waterloo.
